race: Formula 1 Gran Premio de la Ciudad de México 2026

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Welcome to the Race Weekend Podcast, and Mexico City is where the title gets spicy, the pressure rises, and the fans are ready this weekend.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Antonelli is on the edge of his first world title, but he misses Thursday media day with an illness, so the stakes are huge right now.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: He won the United States Grand Prix, yet the title has to wait, so this weekend is the big one for Mercedes and for him and for the team.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Hamilton says Formula One has never had anyone like him, and he is determined to keep racing into his mid forties, which is bold and I respect it.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Mid forties? That is wild, but his Ferrari form is exactly why we have him in third in our list in this episode, and it is a strong call.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Third is top three, and Mexico suits him, so we are not hiding from that pick, because his history there is genuinely good and I can back it.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: His history there is strong, with an average finish near fifth, a best second, and one podium, which is exactly the kind of memory you want for the weekend.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is the kind of circuit memory you want when the air is thin, the straights are long, and a small mistake can cost a lot on this track.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: But our number one is Kimi, and honestly the data is screaming from every angle for Mercedes, because he has been the season story.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Season dominant, many wins, and Mercedes look like the car to beat in this title fight for us, so confidence is high on the win.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Yet his Mexico history is only one race, average sixth, best sixth, and no podium yet, which is the main question mark for the win.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: So we are taking a confidence gamble on a champion who is not the champion yet for the weekend, and I like that because it is bold and fair.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is the line, and I love it, because this is the moment he becomes the champion for everyone, and Mexico can be the stage for it.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: George is our second because Mercedes speed is not just one seat, it is a full package, and he has been consistent all season.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: He has consistent top three finishes and wins again, plus a best fifth at this circuit, so he is always in the conversation.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Three races, average sixth, no podium yet, but he can still strike at the right moment here, especially when the car is right.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: How do you beat that when Lewis and Kimi are both firing, and the pressure is on for him, and the track is so unforgiving?

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: You do not, so we keep him high, but Kimi gets the nod for the win, because the season form is simply too strong to ignore.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Deep cut time, and it is Gasly in tenth for us, a low confidence pick that could still pay off if Alpine find the rhythm.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Low confidence, yes, but Alpine are the best mid field team in our list and score regular points, and Gasly is the one to trust.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Consistent points scorer, and Mexico can reward the bold when the rhythm clicks for him, so we keep him just inside the top ten.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Is that a gamble or a prayer, Paul, this weekend, because I can see the logic, but I need a little more from Alpine on the weekend.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: A prayer with data, and I am happy to take it for the weekend, because mid field moves can change a whole championship picture.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Max is fourth because his recent wins are real, and Mexico history favors him for sure, so he is never far from the front of this grid.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Charles is fifth with Ferrari pace for me and the best Mexico history in our top five, and that history is exactly why he is trusted.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Lando is sixth with McLaren strength for sure, while Oscar, Isack, and Liam round out the top ten with solid points potential.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Now the full top ten, in order, Kimi Antonelli, George Russell, Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc, Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri, Isack Hadjar, Liam Lawson, Pierre Gasly, and enjoy Mexico and have a brilliant Mexico City weekend.
